title: Suspense, lazy loading and error boundaries
summary: Suspense fallbacks, lazy components and code splitting, error boundaries with getDerivedStateFromError and componentDidCatch, what they cannot catch, and resetting them.

sections.title: Suspense
sections.body:
`<Suspense fallback={<Spinner />}>` shows the fallback while anything inside it is **suspended**: a `lazy` component loading its code, a component reading a pending promise with `use`, or a Suspense-enabled data library. When everything is ready, React swaps in the content.

Suspense boundaries can be nested to reveal content in stages. Updates wrapped in a transition keep showing the old content instead of falling back again.

sections.title: lazy and code splitting
sections.body: `const Settings = lazy(() => import("./Settings"))` loads the component's code the first time it renders. The imported module must have a **default export** that is a component. Declare lazy components at the **top level** of a module, never inside another component, or their state resets on every render.

sections.title: Error boundaries
sections.body:
An error boundary catches errors thrown while **rendering**, in lifecycle methods and in constructors of its descendants, and shows a fallback instead of unmounting the whole app. It must be a **class component** with `static getDerivedStateFromError(error)` (returns state to show the fallback) and optionally `componentDidCatch(error, info)` (for logging).

Error boundaries do **not** catch errors in event handlers, in asynchronous code such as `setTimeout` or promise callbacks, in server rendering, or in the boundary itself. Handle those with `try`/`catch` and state, or rethrow them during render.

sections.title: Recovering
sections.body: To let the user retry, add a button in the fallback that clears the error state, ideally after fixing the cause, or give the boundary a `key` that changes (for example the route), which remounts it with fresh state. Libraries such as react-error-boundary wrap this pattern with `resetKeys` and `onReset`.

pitfalls: Writing an error boundary as a function component; there is no hook for it.
Expecting a boundary to catch a click handler error.
A lazy module without a default export.
One boundary around the whole app only, so a small widget error blanks the page.

gotchas.question: An `onClick` handler throws. Does the nearest error boundary show its fallback?
gotchas.answer: No. Error boundaries only catch errors thrown during rendering, lifecycle methods and constructors. The handler error goes to `window.onerror` and the UI stays as it was.

gotchas.question: Which static method switches an error boundary to its fallback?
gotchas.answer: `static getDerivedStateFromError(error)`, which returns the new state. `componentDidCatch` is for side effects such as logging.
